items.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
items.summary: OpenAI is dissolving its standalone robotics team for the second time, but not because it lacks data. General-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can apparently control robots directly, making a dedicated unit unnecessary. The researchers are being redistributed across other teams in what the company frames as a way to accelerate its robotics efforts. The article OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
items.summary: Runway releases its robotics model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses knowledge from video training for robot control and leads the World Action Model category on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 benchmark. It can't yet plan complex action sequences on its own, though. The article Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
items.summary: Jensen Huang likely left Nvidia more because of risky business practices than anything else, a Wall Street Journal report suggests. At the very least, those practices made him enemies internally. The company offered cloud providers billions in financial guarantees for chip purchases, including a planned $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Interim CEO and then-CFO Colette Kress tried to contain the risk, and Huang reportedly didn't like that. The article Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life appeared first on The Decoder .

items.summary: Stanford researchers released Memorilla, an open-source memory system that compresses a document collection into 16 memory tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B. It reaches 84.33% on FactKG using 108x fewer document tokens than full context. The post Stanford Research Open-Sources Memorilla, a Latent Memory Module for Frozen LLMs appeared first on MarkTechPost .
